title: Payoff Interest Day Count by Contract Form — Home Purchase Financing
content:
**Legal department note — day counts of the Home Purchase Financing contract forms for payoff interest**

The payoff interest on a statement turns on the contract form, which follows the date the loan was funded — the date the amount financed was advanced to the seller:

- **Funded on or after 2019-07-01.** The payoff interest is worked out on the actual/365 basis: the unpaid principal times the note rate divided by 100, divided by 365, times the payoff interest days counted from the due date of the last installment paid to the good-through date, counting the good-through date and not that due date, rounded half up to the cent.
- **Funded from 2015-01-01 to 2019-06-30.** Under the contract form of those years, the payoff interest is the unpaid principal times the note rate divided by 100, divided by 360, times the payoff interest days, rounded half up to the cent.
- **Funded before 2015-01-01.** The payoff interest days count both the due date and the good-through date, and the interest is worked out on the actual/365 basis.

| Funding date | Year basis | Days counted |
|---|---|---|
| on or after 2019-07-01 | 365 | good-through date counted, due date not |
| 2015-01-01 to 2019-06-30 | 360 | good-through date counted, due date not |
| before 2015-01-01 | 365 | both the due date and the good-through date |

### One statement under each form (hypothetical: unpaid principal 40000.00, note rate 9.00 percent, last installment paid due 2026-05-01, good through 2026-05-19)

- Funded in 2021: 18 days on 365 — 177.53.
- Funded in 2017: 18 days on 360 — 180.00.
- Funded in 2013: 19 days on 365 — 187.39726…, rounded to 187.40.
